title: Spot prawn, BC coast
text:
Management context
Text in quotation marks is copied exactly as published in DFO’s 2024 Sustainability Survey for Fisheries, including any typos.

Limit reference point, as described by DFO: “The LRP is defined in spawner index units. Using the default formulas in DFO (2008) this would set the LRP at 1.56 spawner index units (40% Bmsy), where Bmsy = 3.9 SI units. https://waves-vagues.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/library-bibliotheque/337043.pdf Explanatory note: The spawner index model is an index of abundance (catch per unit effort based on standardized trap gear). The unit of measure or spawner index is the number of spawners (mature females) per trap.”
Upper stock reference, as described by DFO: “Using the default formulas in DFO (2008) this would set the USR at 3.12 spawner index units (80% Bmsy), where Bmsy =3.9 SI units. https://waves-vagues.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/library-bibliotheque/337043.pdf Explanatory note: The spawner index model is an index of abundance (catch per unit effort based on standardized trap gear). The unit of measure or spawner index is the number of spawners (mature females) per trap.”
Limit used for this project’s indicator: None (no time series compiled)
Management plan, as reported by DFO: “Pacific Region Integrated Fisheries Management Plan Prawn and Shrimp by Trap May 1, 2024 to April 30, 2025.”
Managed by: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO)

title: Methods and data
text: This project combines two open sources into a small, documented database for ten British Columbia stocks. It applies simple written rules to describe each stock’s status, its history, and the gaps in the evidence. It is a learning project by an epidemiologist who is new to fisheries science. It does not replicate DFO’s methods or those of any seafood recommendation program, and it makes no recommendations.

title: Methods and data
text:
How it is built
All steps are R scripts in the GitHub repository, run in order:

01_download.R: downloads the raw files.
04_build_database.R: builds the tidy tables and data dictionary.
05_herring_stripes.R: herring biomass stripes for the Explore page.
06_harmonise_lrp.R: adds the biomass-to-limit indicator and runs the cross-checks.
07_make_figures.R and 08_map_cards.R: figures, map, and cards.
09_render_reports.R: renders one parameterised 2-page PDF per stock.
10_make_site_files.R and 11_make_banner.R: stock pages, card styles, and the home page banner.
quarto render: builds this website.

title: Methods and data
text:
Limitations

RAM Legacy copies published assessments, so the time series end between 2018 and 2021 and may not match DFO’s latest advice.
Limit reference points used for the common indicator are approximate, and some are derived rather than official.
Point estimates only. Assessment uncertainty is not shown.
Map pins mark general areas, not stock boundaries.
National landings data group several BC species together, so they are not used for stock-level conclusions.
Spot prawn and Dungeness crab have no compiled time series; their status here relies entirely on DFO’s survey response.

text: Where the stocks are

title: Ten BC fish stocks. Seventy years of evidence.
text:
Seventy years in one picture

Each row is a stock and each stripe is a year. Red years are below the stock’s limit reference point, the level below which DFO considers serious harm to be occurring. Herring rows show a coast-wide low in the late 1960s and a second, later low on the West Coast of Vancouver Island and the Central Coast. Haida Gwaii herring is the one stock below its limit in its most recent year, which matches its Critical zone in DFO’s 2024 survey.

title: Ten BC fish stocks. Seventy years of evidence.
section: What this is, and what it is not
text:
What this is, and what it is not

It compiles public data from Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) and the RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database into one documented database.
It applies simple, written-down rules to show status, trends, and data gaps for each stock.
It is not an official assessment. It does not reproduce the methodology of any seafood recommendation program, and it makes no recommendations about what to buy or eat.
Assessment time series end between 2018 and 2021, so they can lag DFO’s latest advice.

title: Explore
text:
A Kobe plot places a stock by its biomass (horizontal) and fishing pressure (vertical), both relative to the levels that would produce maximum sustainable yield (MSY). Green means more fish than the MSY level and less fishing than the MSY rate. Red means the opposite. Press Play to draw each stock’s path year by year, or drag the slider.
Only sablefish and Pacific halibut have both ratios in the RAM Legacy database. Halibut fishing-pressure ratios are available for 2000 to 2013 only.

title: Explore
text:
Herring up close

Pacific herring is assessed separately in five major areas. All five show a low period in the late 1960s. The West Coast of Vancouver Island and the Central Coast had a second low period in the mid to late 2000s. Haida Gwaii spent most years after 2000 below its limit.

title: About
text:
I’m Emma Branch, an epidemiologist and data analyst, and a PhD candidate at the University of British Columbia. I mostly work in R, SAS, and SQL, and use Quarto, Shiny, and leaflet when the results need to be readable by actual humans.
I’m new to fisheries science. The quickest way I know to learn a field is to get my hands on its data, so I built this to get to grips with the basics (stock assessment, reference points, and DFO’s Precautionary Approach). It also let me apply the habits I’ve picked up in health research: a tidy database with a data dictionary, rule-based checks, parameterised reports, and being upfront about what the data can’t tell you.
This is an exploratory personal project. It isn’t an official assessment, it doesn’t reproduce any seafood recommendation program’s methods, and it makes no recommendations. Any mistakes are mine, and corrections are very welcome through the GitHub repository.

Text in quotation marks is copied exactly as published in DFO’s 2024 Sustainability Survey for Fisheries, including any typos.

Limit reference point, as described by DFO: “0.3SBo (unfished spawning biomass) or 14,854 tonnes* (estimates are updated annually) *value reported from the 2023 stock assessment, implemented for 2023/24 fishery”
Upper stock reference, as described by DFO: “Implementation of USRs occurred through the 2023/24 Pacific Herring IFMP. For the CC stock, the USR for was set at the average spawning biomass during the productive period (1990-1999). Provisional USRs are considered spawning biomass objectives in the MSE process and are not considered equivalent to the upper control point of the harvest control rule.”
Limit used for this project’s indicator: 0.3 x unfished spawning biomass (SSB0 from the 2018 assessment in RAM)
Management plan, as reported by DFO: “2023/24 Pacific Herring IFMP - November 7, 2023 - November 6, 2024”
Managed by: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO)
